samples.summary: Clipboard sanitizer re-implements block-style validation that `model/crdt-attrs.ts` already owns as the single source of truth
samples.evidence: `clipboard.ts` declares its own `ALIGNMENTS = ['left','center','right','justify']` (line 49) and its own numeric block-style field list inside `sanitizeBlockStyle` (`['lineHeight','marginTop','marginBottom','textIndent','marginLeft']`, ~line 183). `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts` already exports `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS`, `isBlockAlignment()` and `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` and its header states the reason verbatim: "That contract used to be maintained by copy-paste; it lives here instead so there is exactly one encoding of a block style on the wire." The backend's untrusted-input validator (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:335-362 assertValidBlockStyle`) does reuse exactly those exports. The new sanitizer becomes a third, hand-maintained copy of the same allowlist/number rules — precisely the drift crdt-attrs exists to prevent. Same pattern for the block-type allowlist (`BLOCK_TYPES`, line 45) which restates `BlockType` in `model/types.ts:39` with no type-level link, so a new block type silently becomes unpasteable.

samples.summary: The heading-memory provenance rules exceed the issue's stated "smallest possible model change" and its explicit split Non-goal, now spread over four predicates in three layers
samples.evidence: The task doc's Non-goals say "Splitting a bulleted heading (Enter) — the new item stays a plain list item, as today", then amends itself in-place to carve out the offset-0 exception implemented here (`splitMovesHeadingMemory`). The single retained-`headingLevel` model choice has now grown into four separate rules — `unlistedBlockType` (model/types.ts), `splitMovesHeadingMemory` + `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (store/block-helpers.ts), `foldedHeadingLevel` (view/text-editor.ts) — each duplicated into the Yorkie tree writer, plus an `insertBlocks` workaround for `Doc.splitBlock`'s empty-list-item short-circuit. Worth confirming this is the intended cost of the retained-level model rather than a signal that the memory belongs in a field whose lifetime does not have to be re-derived at every text-moving operation.

samples.summary: Entry-export parity is enforced by regex-scanning source text at test time rather than by a type/build-level check
samples.evidence: `blockHelperExports()` reads `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts` with `readFileSync` and matches `export { ... } from '...'` with a regex. This encodes an invariant about module structure as a text assertion: it breaks on formatting (multi-line clauses with comments, `export *`, a differently quoted specifier) and passes for a helper exported under a different re-export form. A shared `export { ... } from './store/block-helpers.js'` barrel imported by both entries, or a type-level assertion, would make the invariant structural instead of textual.

samples.summary: `foldedHeadingLevel` sits in the view layer while its sibling provenance predicates live in the store layer
samples.evidence: `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` and `splitMovesHeadingMemory` are exported from `src/store/block-helpers.ts` (and re-exported from both entries so `YorkieDocStore` can share them), while the third rule for the same invariant, `foldedHeadingLevel`, is a module-private function in `src/view/text-editor.ts`. If any other paste/fold path (slides text box, table-cell paste, DOCX import merge) ever needs the same rule it cannot reach it, which is the drift the other two helpers were extracted to avoid.

finding.summary: Clipboard sanitizer re-implements block-style validation that `model/crdt-attrs.ts` already owns as the single source of truth
finding.evidence: `clipboard.ts` declares its own `ALIGNMENTS = ['left','center','right','justify']` (line 49) and its own numeric block-style field list inside `sanitizeBlockStyle` (`['lineHeight','marginTop','marginBottom','textIndent','marginLeft']`, ~line 183). `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts` already exports `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS`, `isBlockAlignment()` and `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` and its header states the reason verbatim: "That contract used to be maintained by copy-paste; it lives here instead so there is exactly one encoding of a block style on the wire." The backend's untrusted-input validator (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:335-362 assertValidBlockStyle`) does reuse exactly those exports. The new sanitizer becomes a third, hand-maintained copy of the same allowlist/number rules — precisely the drift crdt-attrs exists to prevent. Same pattern for the block-type allowlist (`BLOCK_TYPES`, line 45) which restates `BlockType` in `model/types.ts:39` with no type-level link, so a new block type silently becomes unpasteable.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location verified as described. clipboard.ts:45-49 declares its own BLOCK_TYPES and ALIGNMENTS allowlists, and sanitizeBlockStyle (clipboard.ts:178-191) re-lists the numeric block-style fields inline; the file's imports (clipboard.ts:1-9) never touch crdt-attrs. model/crdt-attrs.ts:22-47 already exports BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS, isBlockAlignment() and BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS with identical members, and its header (lines 8-10) states verbatim that the contract "used to be maintained by copy-paste; it lives here instead so there is exactly one encoding of a block style on the wire." That reuse point is already the established one for untrusted input: backend assertValidBlockStyle (docs-content.controller.ts:335-362) consumes exactly those three exports. clipboard's BLOCK_TYPES likewise restates the BlockType union (types.ts:39) with no `satisfies readonly BlockType[]` link, so a new block type would silently be unpasteable. Assignment-site typing catches field removals but not additions, so the drift risk is real. This is a duplication/reuse fit violation in this lens's lane (existing in-package module owns the allowlist; new code is a third hand-maintained copy), not a line-level correctness bug, and no guard elsewhere makes it moot.

finding.summary: `splitMovesHeadingMemory` (offset-0 split moves the remembered level) contradicts the plan's stated Non-goal on splitting
finding.evidence: The spec's Non-goals say: "Splitting a bulleted heading (Enter) — the new item stays a plain list item, as today. ... `applySplitBlock` keeps dropping `headingLevel` for a non-`heading` split half. Only the block that was actually bulleted remembers." The diff introduces an exception (offset 0 moves the memory), and to honour it adds a shared predicate plus new CRDT writes in `YorkieDocStore.splitBlock` (`removeStyleByPath(['headingLevel'])` and stamping the attr onto the new node) — new collaborative-edit surface not covered by the plan. Either the plan's Non-goal should be amended explicitly, or this exception belongs in a follow-up; as written the diff both asserts the Non-goal (docs.md) and carves an exception into it.

verdict.reason: The mechanism exists (block-helpers.ts:290-302 predicate, applySplitBlock:260-266, yorkie-doc-store.ts:2054-2068/2099-2104 CRDT writes), but the claimed spec contradiction is not present. The plan's Non-goals section itself explicitly amends the split Non-goal: docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:59-65 documents the offset-0 exception by name ("splitMovesHeadingMemory states the rule and both stores honour it"), which also covers the second-store/CRDT write the finding calls uncovered. The canonical design doc states the general drop rule (docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-177) and the exception in the same subsystem file (:179-188), naming the shared predicate and explicitly describing YorkieDocStore.splitBlock's removeStyleByPath + stamping. The finding's own requested remedy ("the plan's Non-goal should be amended explicitly") is already met, so there is no unamended Non-goal violation and no missing/parallel design doc.

finding.summary: DOCX `<w:pStyle>` heading-level coercion is unrelated hardening, in an area the plan lists as a non-goal
finding.evidence: The plan's Non-goals include "DOCX/PPTX export of a bulleted heading's `pStyle`", and the diff nonetheless edits `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` to `Number()`/`trunc`/clamp the level plus three new tests, motivated by clipboard-injection hardening rather than by the un-list regression. It also duplicates a clamp that already exists for the same value in `packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:108` (`Math.min(6, Math.max(1, block.headingLevel ?? 1))`) — a shared `clampHeadingLevel` (one already exists in `serialize/markdown.ts`) would be the reuse-friendly home.

verdict.reason: The finding's two blocking grounds are both contradicted by the repo. (a) Non-goal: the plan's non-goal (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:66) is exporting a *bulleted heading's* pStyle; the exporter still gates on `block.type === 'heading'` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:205-208), so a list-item's remembered level is never emitted — the non-goal is honored. The added `toHeadingStyleId` (docx-style-map.ts:139-144) only validates the level for real heading blocks, and it neither truncs nor clamps as claimed: it returns `undefined` so the element is dropped. It is also not "unrelated": docs/design/docs/docs.md:225-235 documents it as the sink-side counterpart of the clipboard sanitizer this change adds (clipboard.ts:325-331), and docs-docx-import-export.md:440 records it in the canonical doc — no parallel doc. (b) Duplication: named-styles.ts:105-110 clamps into the internal `heading-N` catalog, serialize/markdown.ts:128-132 clamps a private `#`-repeat count, and toHeadingStyleId rejects to drop the OOXML attribute; sharing one `clampHeadingLevel` would change the DOCX fallback semantics, so this is a refactor preference, not a reinvented module. The residual (a ~6-line documented defensive check plus tests) is at most `minor` under this lens, which never blocks.
